### 2026-07-30 — BUT-1724 RE-REVIEW after automated fixes: what actually changed, and a test-double aliasing hazard the CollectionReference refactor introduced [Pattern discovered]

Second pass over the same scoped fileset as the entry above, re-read from the
WORKING TREE (`git status` shows all nine files as ` M`, index and worktree agree).

**What the "automated fixes" actually changed in my scope: one thing.**
`compute-feature-retention.test.ts` grew a 7th case, `shoppedProbeFailureDegrades`
("shopped probe failure (missing index) degrades to false, run completes"), plus the
harness change that makes it possible: `failProbeFor` now matches on EITHER
`args.source` OR a new `args.failFlag`, because a subcollection source's path is
`users/{uid}/{sub}` and could never match on a feature-flag name alone. Both
production files (`compute-feature-retention.ts` md5 `c7c7760001a46bea8bb7eb6cbf4612b2`,
`on-profile-updated.ts` md5 `7cc2acc50a2f35385526b66cefa5143c`) and
`on-profile-updated.test.ts` (`157593706a0206bd1de17a36fc800b57`) are byte-unchanged
from the start of this pass to the end. The three Medium/Low findings from the first
pass are all still OPEN — nothing was "fixed", a test was added.

**The mid-review byte drift fired again, and the existing principle caught it.**
I hashed the five functions files before running anything and again afterwards;
`compute-feature-retention.test.ts` moved `f7bb93d7…` → `8f67bac2…` DURING the pass
(the 6-case version was what I first diffed and ran at 6/6). Re-diffed, re-read the
harness, re-typechecked, re-ran at 7/7, hashed before and after that run (stable).
Also honoured the shared-scratchpad rule — the scratchpad already held
`_run_test.bat`..`_run_test5.bat`, `rt.bat`, `mutate.js` from other sessions, so my
runner was `_cfs_friends_$$.bat` and my harness `_cfs_mutate_1724.js`, and I checked
the printed suite names matched what I asked for.

**New hazard, and it is a consequence of the accepted fix.** `paginatedDualUpdate`
now takes ONE `CollectionReference` and calls `.where()` on it twice. In
`on-profile-updated.test.ts`'s `makeFakeDb`, `collectionRef(name)` builds a SINGLE
mutable `q` (`makeQuery` closes over `predicate`/`ordered`/`limitN`/`afterKey` and
every builder returns `q`), so the second `.where()` OVERWRITES the first's predicate
— whereas the old name-based signature called `db.collection(name)` separately per leg
and got two independent doubles. It passes today for a benign reason: `async get()`
contains no `await` before it filters `activity`, so leg A's page-1 rows are captured
synchronously during array-literal evaluation, before leg B's `.where()` runs. The
break is on page 2 — leg A's `startAfter(...).limit().get()` would re-read with leg B's
predicate. Consequence, and the reason this is worth a principle: the suite's headline
claim ("neither result set is ever fully held in memory", "cursor neither skips nor
revisits") is UNPROVEN for `paginatedDualUpdate`, because there is no `>BATCH_LIMIT`
dual-field fixture and one could not be written against this double. Fix belongs in the
double (return a fresh object from every builder call), not in the SUT.

Verification I did that the first pass did not:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` on `functions/` → exit 0 (twice, before and after the drift).
- `npm run test:compute-feature-retention` → **7/7**; grepped the run's own output to
  prove the new injection FIRES rather than passing on an empty fixture:
  `{"flag":"shopped","userId":"uIdx","err":{},"severity":"WARNING","message":"feature_retention_probe_failed"}`.
  The case is non-vacuous by construction too — it seeds
  `users/uIdx/unified_shopping_lists` in-day so the probe WOULD answer true, and then
  asserts `shopped === false` with `mealPlanned === true` alongside.
- `npm run test:on-profile-updated` → 6/6, and re-mutation-proved BOTH new tests with
  the CRLF-safe harness (occurrence count asserted == 1, `out !== s` asserted, md5
  restore verified): reverting the personal leg to `db.collection(Collections.unifiedShoppingLists)`
  → `4/6 passed, 2 failed`, i.e. the BUT-1724 case AND the positive control inside the
  avatar-only case ("control: a name change DOES reach the same personal list:
  expected \"Annika\", got \"Anna\""); reverting the probe to
  `.collection(Collections.unifiedShoppingLists ? "shopping_lists" : "x")` →
  `5/6 passed, 1 failed`, exactly the targeted case.
- Premise re-checks the first pass asserted but I re-ran from source:
  `firestore.rules:394` = `match /unified_shopping_lists/{listId}` under
  `users/{userId}` and NO top-level match (grep of the whole rules file: only
  `unified_shared_shopping_lists:1602` and `user_shared_shopping_lists:1685` are
  top-level) — so both the SUT comment and the test's "ghost" fixture rest on a
  verified fact. `firestore.indexes.json` `fieldOverrides` dumped in full: no entry for
  `unified_shopping_lists` at all, so the equality+`__name__` ASC propagation legs and
  the `updatedAt`-only range probe are auto-indexed; no index deploy is required by this
  diff. `unified_shopping_list.dart:594-622` writes `ownerId`, `ownerDisplayName`,
  `lastActivityByUserId`, `lastActivityByDisplayName` and `updatedAt` as a `Timestamp`,
  so all three newly-live queries match real fields — this fix is not another dead read.
- `node scripts/check-test-registration.js` → OK, 118 registered, 4 accepted-debt warns.
  No new export in `index.ts`, so the `app-check-enforcement.test.ts` triple does not apply.
- NUL/binary check on all five functions files → clean.
- `flutter analyze` on the four Dart files → "No issues found!" (60s), which also proves
  no import or private method was orphaned by deleting `getRecentShoppingCollaborators`.
- `flutter test test/unit/services/unified/unified_friends_service_test.dart` → 20/20.
- Repo-wide grep for `getRecentShoppingCollaborators`: live checkout clean; hits only in
  `.claude/worktrees/*` (other sessions) and in agent knowledge archives.
- `FirestoreCollections.userShoppingLists`: exactly one Dart reference,
  `firebase_data_export_repository_shopping_test.dart:152`, and I READ it — it is the

- Confirmed the docstring's accepted gap 2 again from source: the personal branches of

New Low noted this pass: `failProbeFor.flag` is now overloaded — line 558 passes a
SOURCE name (`"cook_snaps"`) and line 661 passes a FEATURE FLAG (`"shopped"`). Works,
but a future case will guess the wrong one and get a silently-not-injected failure that
looks like a passing test. Rename to `failProbeFor.match` or split the two fields.

Folded into the principles file as: a new bullet in "Test seams, emulator infra &

### 2026-07-30 — BUT-1706/1721/1732/1746 re-review: shopping/account GDPR export + shared-list rules coverage [Pattern discovered]

Re-review of 11 files after automated fixes. Verdict PASS. What I actually ran:

- `bash tools/check_null_filter.sh` (no args, whole `lib`+`test`) → exit 0, so all four
  BUT-1746 sites are fixed. Then two scratch fixtures: a file whose only hit is a
  CONSTRUCTION site → exit 1 with the remediation block; a file whose only hit is a
  `//` COMMENT → exit 0. The `-H` comment on line 40-43 of the script is load-bearing and
  correct: with one file argument grep drops the filename, and the comment filter anchors
  past a `path:line:` prefix.
- `npx lefthook validate` → "All good"; `npx lefthook dump | grep -A5 null-filter-guard`
  → glob `*.dart`, priority 8 (unique; 1-8 all distinct). I deliberately did NOT run
  `npx lefthook run pre-commit --command null-filter-guard`: nothing was staged and 39
  files were unstaged, so lefthook's hide step would have stashed the whole live worktree
  next to a parallel session.
- `npx ts-node src/__tests__/shared-shopping-lists-rules.test.ts` against the running
  emulator → **39/39 passed**, file md5 `cf0a9292…` identical before and after. The new
  legs are SSL26-31 (read gate incl. the revoked-member deny), SSL32-34 (create
  conjuncts), SSL35-36 (owner-only delete), SSL37-39 (query path). Cross-checked every
  one against `firestore.rules:1602-1653` by hand.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in `functions/` → exit 0.
- `flutter test` on the three Dart suites via a uniquely-named `_cfs_review_$$.bat`
  → +112 all passed (query 20 + routing 55 + export 36 + 1 teardown line).
- `dart analyze` on all 6 reviewed lib/test Dart files + `shopping_list_permission_guards.dart`
  → "No issues found!".

**Emulator-corpus shelf life on a limit()-scoped deny test (new).** SSL38 ("an edit member
CANNOT run an UNFILTERED collection query") is denied only because `query-foreign`
(owned by STRANGER, EDITOR absent from `memberPermissions`) is inside
`.limit(200)`. I dumped the corpus with
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer owner" "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/projects/butlery-shared-shopping-lists-test/databases/(default)/documents/unified_shared_shopping_lists?pageSize=300"`
— **47 docs after 6 runs**, of which 18 are `create-{seat,absent,at-cap}-<RUN>` (3 new per
run, the per-run token being exactly what makes them accumulate). Those sort BEFORE
`query-foreign` by `__name__`, so at ~200 docs the foreign doc leaves the window and
`assertFails` starts FAILING. Direction is safe (red, not a false green) and CI restarts
the emulator each job, so it is a local-dev slow burn — Low. Fix: name the unreadable
fixture so it sorts first (`00-query-foreign`) or drop the limit on that one test.
Without the `Authorization: Bearer owner` header the REST read is itself rules-evaluated
and returns 403 `false for 'list' @ L1622` — which is incidentally a second, independent
confirmation of the read rule.

**The file moved under the review again, and this time it was an IMPROVEMENT.**
`md5sum -c` after the Dart run flagged `shopping_repository_routing_module_test.dart`
(`3e16801d…` → `b947a91c…`, mtime 13:54). Re-`git diff` showed a parallel session had
strengthened the new BUT-1706 test: the old assertion was `name == 'Veckans handla'`
only, which holds whether or not the guard exists (the offline payload never carries
`name`); the new one adds `items isEmpty`, which is the falsifiable half (without the
guard the append reaches `appendPayload`'s arrayUnion and the row lands). Re-ran the suite
on the new bytes → **56/56 passed**, hash stable across that run. Lesson: a mid-review
byte change is not automatically someone's mutation proof — re-diff, re-run, report
against the new bytes either way. `md5sum ... | tee before.md5` + `md5sum -c before.md5`
is the cheapest detector because it names the offending file.

**Non-vacuity without mutating production.** I did not comment out
`_offline.requireOfflineWritableMutation(live, mutated)` to prove the new test reddens —
too dangerous with a parallel session in the same checkout. It is provable by
construction instead: the test asserts `isA<ArgumentError>()` whose message
`contains('dropped silently')`, and that literal exists nowhere but the new
`requireOfflineWritableMutation`. A test asserting a NEW exception type + a NEW message
literal cannot pass against the pre-fix code.

**Verified the "no live mutator trips the new guard" claim rather than trusting it.**
`requireOfflineWritableMutation` throws when a mutator changes any key outside
`{items} ∪ _writableActivityKeys` (and outside `privilegedKeys`, which are dropped by
design). Traced every mutator: `ShoppingItemOperationsModule._withItems` →
`copyWith(items, updatedAt, lastActivityAt, lastActivityByUserId,
lastActivityByDisplayName)`; the model's `addItem`/`removeItem`/`toggleItemBought` add
`syncStatus`, which is in `toJson()` but NOT in `toFirestore()`, so it is invisible to the
guard. `UnifiedShoppingList.toFirestore()` emits all 20 keys unconditionally (nulls
included), which also closes the obvious hole in the guard — a key cleared to null still
appears in `after.keys`, so no drop goes undetected. And the throw is contained:
`UnifiedShoppingService.mutateSharedList` has a bare `catch (e)` tail that converts it to
`false` + a `shoppingFailureMessage`, so it cannot escape to the UI uncaught.

**The BUT-1706 required-fields mirror is unfalsifiable through the public API, and that
is fine.** `validateRequiredFields` checks `containsKey` only (matching the rule's
`hasRequiredFields`), and `toFirestore()` always emits all five keys — so the widened
`collaborativeCreateRequiredFields` can never fire for a real `UnifiedShoppingList`. The
routing test pins the LIST passed to the injected validator, not a refusal, which is the
only honest thing it can do. Don't file it as vacuous; do not "strengthen" it into
asserting a throw.

**Residual PII in export SECTION bodies (Medium, pre-existing, out of the reviewed
fileset).** BUT-1732 fixed the ROOT: `data_export_service.dart:266-287` now DERIVES
`warnings[].message` and never copies `value['error']` through. `social_export_manager`
and `activity_export_manager` were converted to stable sentences + `error_code`. But
`content_export_manager.dart` (12 sites) and `preferences_export_manager.dart` (9 sites)
still `return {'error': e.toString()}` inside their sections, so a raw Firestore string —
`blocks/<uid>_<otherUid>`, a `create_composite` URL naming `memberPermissions.<uid>` and
the project id — is still in the delivered bundle, one level down. The new code comments
say so explicitly, and the test fixture `_LeakyPreferencesExportRepository` deliberately
asserts that section-level leak as its PREMISE. Follow-up ticket, not a blocker for this
diff.

Also noted (Low): `tools/check_null_filter.sh` bans only `isNotEqualTo`/`isEqualTo`, but
`cloud_firestore`'s `query.dart` guards EVERY operator with `if (arg != null)` — so
`arrayContains: null`, `whereIn: null`, `isLessThan: null` are the same silent
unfiltered-read footgun and pass the guard. Widening the alternation is a one-line change.

Folded into the principles file as: the emulator-corpus/limit() shelf-life clause on the
"emulator KEEPS data across runs" bullet, a read-only substitute (`lefthook validate` +
`lefthook dump` + direct script fixtures) on the "prove a lefthook glob" bullet, and the
"the mid-review change may be an improvement" clause + the `md5sum -c` detector on the
"file can change UNDER the review" bullet.

### 2026-07-30 — BUT-1706/1721/1732/1746 shopping+GDPR re-review: a live mutation faked a Critical [Pattern discovered]

Scope handed over (11 files, "after automated fixes"): `tools/check_null_filter.sh` (new),
`lefthook.yml`, `functions/src/__tests__/shared-shopping-lists-rules.test.ts`, the three
GDPR export files (`data_export_service.dart`, `social_export_manager.dart`,
`activity_export_manager.dart`) + its test, `shopping_repository_routing_module.dart`,
`shopping_offline_write_module.dart`, and two shopping module tests.

Verification actually run (all against recorded `git hash-object` blobs, identical before
and after every suite):
- `flutter test` on the three Dart suites (data-export + shopping query + shopping
  routing) via a uniquely-named batch wrapper (`_cfs_shopgdpr_30152.bat`) → **112 passed**.
- `npx ts-node src/__tests__/shared-shopping-lists-rules.test.ts` against the live
  emulator → **39/39 passed** (the 13 new SSL26-SSL39 cases included).
- `node functions/scripts/check-test-registration.js` → OK, 118 registered, 38 rules
  suites; `npx tsc --noEmit` in `functions/` → clean.
- `dart analyze --fatal-infos` on all 9 Dart files → "No issues found!".
- `npx lefthook validate` → "All good"; `npx lefthook dump` resolves `null-filter-guard`
  with `glob: '*.dart'`, `priority: 8`.
- `bash tools/check_null_filter.sh` in three modes (whole tree, single positive fixture,
  comment-only fixture).

**The near-miss.** The whole-tree guard run printed two violations in
`lib/repositories/firebase/modules/shopping_repository_query_module.dart:72,229` —
`.where('memberPermissions.$uid', isNotEqualTo: null)`, i.e. the exact BUT-1746 defect the
commit claims to fix, sitting three lines under a WHY-comment that says the code uses
`isNull: false`. That file was NOT in the handed-over fileset and `git status` at session
start showed it clean, so the natural write-up was a Critical ("the fix was never applied
to the production file; only its test and comments were updated"). Disambiguators that
settled it in ~60 seconds instead:
- `git status --porcelain -- <file>` RE-RUN → ` M` (the session-start snapshot was stale).
- `git show HEAD:<file> | grep -n` → HEAD holds `isNull: false` on both lines, i.e. the
  worktree carried an UNCOMMITTED REGRESSION against a correct HEAD, which is the shape of
  a mutation proof, not of an unfinished fix.
- `stat -c '%y'` → modified 14:27:14 against a 14:28:03 clock: seconds old, mid-review.
- Polling on CONTENT (`grep -q "isNull: false"` in a loop) → restored on the FIRST poll.
Re-ran the query-module suite against the restored bytes (hash `eab424313…`) → 20/20 pass.
So: a parallel session's non-vacuity proof for the BUT-1746 tests. Third instance in one
day (both realtime services earlier), and the first where the mutated file was OUTSIDE the
review's fileset and was surfaced by a newly-added GUARD SCRIPT rather than by a red test.

**SSL38's measured shelf life.** REST-enumerated the emulator corpus with
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer owner" ".../unified_shared_shopping_lists?pageSize=300"`:
56 docs, of which 27 are `create-{seat,absent,at-cap}-<RUN>` (9 runs x 3 persisted
creates; the three new deny-side creates persist nothing). Ordered by `__name__`,
`create-*` < `del-editor` < **`query-foreign`** < `query-mine` < `read-*`, so the ONE doc
EDITOR cannot read sits at position ~29 of the `.limit(200)` window, and every `create-*`
doc IS readable by EDITOR (`validListBody` seats them). At +3 docs/run the unreadable
fixture leaves the window after ~57 more runs and SSL38's `assertFails` starts failing —
red, not a false green, but a dated trap. Same defect the knowledge file already predicted
for this exact doc id; it was not fixed in this pass.

**GDPR export chokepoint.** `data_export_service.dart:266-287` now keys the bundle-level
warning on `error` OR `error_code`, derives its own token
(`'${entry.key}-export-failed'`) and DERIVES the message instead of copying
`value['error']`. That is the right defence, and the diff's own comment is honest that
`content_export_manager.dart` (12 sites) and `preferences_export_manager.dart` (10 sites)
still `return {'error': e.toString()}` — those raw strings remain inside the exported
SECTION body (not the root), so the residual is narrowed, not closed. `_declaresTruncation`
was checked for false positives: no client Dart code writes a `truncated`/`*_truncated`
field into any exported document, and `llm_response_samples` (which does carry one) is not
an export section.

**The offline whitelist enforcement was checked for the opposite failure.** A refusal
computed from `mutated.toFirestore().keys` breaks every legitimate write if the model
stamps a derived field. Read `UnifiedShoppingList.toFirestore()` (no derived/computed
keys) and every live mutator: `_withItems` in `shopping_item_operations_module.dart:98-111`
touches items + exactly the four `_activityFieldKeys`, and `contributorUserIds` is not in
`toFirestore()` at all — so `requireOfflineWritableMutation` cannot fire on any current
path, as its docstring claims. `validateRequiredFields` is `containsKey`-only
(`permission_validation_mixin.dart:290-292`), so widening the create mirror to `items` +
`createdAt` cannot refuse an empty-but-present array/map, i.e. it stays a superset of the
rule's `hasRequiredFields` rather than becoming stricter.

Findings filed: 4 Medium/Low, nothing Critical/High. (1) Medium — SSL38 shelf life above,

### 2026-07-30 — Sprint 2026-07-30b RESCUE pass: 5-file staged review (BUT-1724 + BUT-1692), no marker covered a byte of it [Pattern discovered]

Dispatched as a FIRST review, not a re-check: the sprint held its own commit after its own
outcome verification failed four tickets on data-safety, and the live
`cloud-functions-done.marker` was from 2026-07-29 over a different fileset. Scope:
`analytics/compute-feature-retention.ts`, `social/on-profile-updated.ts`,
`admin/reset-user-data.ts`, `notifications/send-notification.ts`,
`middleware/rate_limiter.ts`. **Verdict: pass** (two Mediums + two Lows, all pre-existing
or out-of-diff; nothing Critical/High introduced).

**Cross-pass hashing paid off again, and gave the opposite answer this time.** Passes 2-4
of BUT-1724 recorded `on-profile-updated.ts` md5 `7cc2acc50a2f35385526b66cefa5143c` and
`compute-feature-retention.ts` `c7c7760001a46bea8bb7eb6cbf4612b2`; both STILL match, and
`reset-user-data.ts` still matches pass 3's `9575e7d7cf3694a8da118b5f918867e5` in the
worktree. So the production SUTs have not moved in four passes. What DID move is the TEST:
`on-profile-updated.test.ts` went `157593706a0206bd1de17a36fc800b57` ->
`6c6691b54035329ffdc93cb9e9a4bcc0`. That is pass-3's Finding (1) — the mutable test double
— actually being fixed. Lesson: hash the TESTS as well as the SUTs across passes, because a
pass whose only movement is in a fixture reads as "nothing was fixed" if you only hash
production files. `git status --porcelain` showed every scoped file `M ` (index == worktree),
so there was no `MM` trap.

**`on-profile-updated.ts` — the query-shape change is NOT a collectionGroup, and that is the
finding worth recording.** The brief warned it might be one (a collectionGroup query is not
user-scoped unless a rule or filter makes it so). It is not: the leg is
`db.collection("users").doc(userId).collection(Collections.unifiedShoppingLists)` with
`userId` bound to `event.params.userId`, i.e. the trigger's own doc-id path segment. Every
read and write is inside that one user's subtree, so cross-user reach is structurally
impossible, and no `fieldOverrides` entry is needed — `firestore.indexes.json` mentions
neither `unified_shopping_lists` nor `unified_shared_shopping_lists` at all, so no
single-field EXEMPTION exists either and the auto index covers equality + `__name__ ASC`.
Verified the fields are real, not assumed: `UnifiedShoppingList.toFirestore()`
(`lib/models/unified/unified_shopping_list.dart:595`) writes `ownerId`, `ownerDisplayName`,
`lastActivityByUserId`, `lastActivityByDisplayName` and `updatedAt` as a `Timestamp` on the
SAME model for personal and collaborative lists — which is also what makes the retention
probe's `updatedAt` range filter type-correct (`shopping_template_operations_module.dart`
uses `serverTimestamp()`, also a Timestamp; no ISO-string writer on that path).
`firestore.rules:394` has the `users/{userId}/unified_shopping_lists/{listId}` match with an
`items` child, confirming the path holds client-written data. Retry semantics: the trigger
is `onDocumentUpdated` with no `retry: true`, every step is independently `.catch`ed, and
the writes are same-value-idempotent, so a re-delivery is a no-op.

**Real remaining gap on that same function (Medium, pre-existing, out of diff).** The
shopping legs propagate only LIST-level names. `UnifiedShoppingItem` carries
`addedByDisplayName` and `lastModifiedByDisplayName` (`unified_shopping_item.dart:212,236`),
stored both in the per-list `items` subcollection and in the embedded `items` array on the
list doc — and `account-deletion-cascade.ts:624,629` scrubs exactly those two on erasure.
So erasure covers item-level stamps and propagation does not: after a rename, every
"X la till ..." row keeps the old name forever, on personal and shared lists alike. This is
the `PROPAGATION coverage is not ERASURE coverage` principle running in the reverse
direction, and it is now folded in there with the fix shape
(`collectionGroup("items").where("addedByUserId","==",uid)` + a `COLLECTION_GROUP`
fieldOverride; the embedded array copy is not queryable and needs read-modify-write).

**`rate_limiter.ts` — the file the plan called "(read-only reference)" and then modified.**
One hunk: `logRateLimitViolation` now resolves its handle via `getFirestore()` instead of
`admin.firestore()`. Production behaviour is byte-identical (`firestoreForTest` is `null`
-> `admin.firestore()`), and grepping `__setFirestoreForTest` across `functions/src`
excluding `__tests__` returns only the declaration — no production caller, so the audit row
cannot land anywhere but `system_events`. The handle is resolved INSIDE the try and the
helper is best-effort (`catch` -> `logger.warn`), so a Firestore failure still cannot turn a
rate-limit denial into a 500. `getGlobalLimits`/`checkGlobalLimit` (lines 516, 563-564)
remain on `admin.firestore()` — the seam is still partial, unchanged, fine.

**`send-notification.ts`.** `preflightNotificationBatch`'s seam went `rateLimit?: typeof
checkRateLimit` -> `enforce?: typeof enforceRateLimit`, and the hand-rolled
`resource-exhausted` throw is gone, so the batch path now writes the `system_events`
`rate_limit_violation` row. `MAX_BATCH_NOTIFICATIONS` exported and pinned to
`RATE_LIMIT_CONFIGS.sendNotificationBatch.maxTokens` by `rate-limiter-daily-cap.test.ts`
(14/14). `checkRateLimit` is still imported and still used by the single-send callable, so
no unused-import build break. The docstrings now state the single-send hole (BUT-1763)
explicitly instead of implying the family is uniformly audited — the over-claim flagged in
an earlier pass is closed in prose as well as in code. Still true: no Dart caller of
`sendNotificationBatch` exists in `lib/`, so the new write-per-denial stream into a
TTL-less `system_events` is ~zero volume today.

**`reset-user-data.ts` — comment-only, and the comment's claim about code checks out.**
`deleteWithSubcollections` does `db.collection(name).listDocuments()` -> `deleteDocRecursive`
per doc -> `listCollections()` at every depth, so "a subcollection missing from this list is
still wiped" is true for TOP-LEVEL targets too, not only nested ones — worth checking,
because the sibling NON-recursive `deleteCollection` lives in the same file and would have
made the sentence false. `unified_shared_shopping_lists` IS present as its own top-level
target; the top-level `unified_shopping_lists` entry is a harmless legacy no-op.

**Suites run against the staged bytes, all green:** `test:on-profile-updated` 6/6 (incl. the

### 2026-07-30 — BUT-1761 review: the `shopped` collaborative leg (analytics/) [Pattern discovered]

Reviewed `functions/src/analytics/compute-feature-retention.ts`,
`functions/src/__tests__/compute-feature-retention.test.ts`, `firestore.indexes.json`.
The change adds a SIXTH probe behind the existing `shopped` flag:
`unified_shared_shopping_lists` where `lastActivityByUserId == uid` AND an `updatedAt`
day range, OR-ed with the personal-subcollection leg. Declares the composite
(`lastActivityByUserId` ASC, `updatedAt` ASC, COLLECTION scope) and a test that asserts
that declaration against the real `firestore.indexes.json`.

Verified the premise end-to-end rather than from the docstring: `Collections
.unifiedSharedShoppingLists === "unified_shared_shopping_lists"`;
`UnifiedShoppingList.toFirestore()` writes `updatedAt` as a real `Timestamp` (not an ISO
string) and `lastActivityByUserId` alongside it; every model mutator (`addItem`,
`removeItem`, `updateItem`/`toggleItemBought`, `clearBoughtItems`, `uncheckAllItems`)
bumps both in one `copyWith`; the transactional tick path
(`ShoppingRepositoryRoutingModule.mutateCollaborativeList` → `transaction.set(...,
merge:true)` of `mutated.toFirestore()`) persists both, and
`ListItemOperations.toggleItemBought` passes a non-null `userId`. Offline replay keeps
them too — `ShoppingOfflineWriteModule._writableActivityKeys` includes `updatedAt` and
`lastActivityByUserId`. So the leg really does fire on a shop-aisle tick.

Ran `npm run test:compute-feature-retention` → 11/11 PASS. `npm run build` → clean.
`test:compute-feature-retention` is registered in `package.json` and `CI_EXCLUDE` is empty,
so the suite runs in the real CI lane.

**Mutation testing (the finding).** Two mutations, each restored and the diffstat
re-checked (93 insertions / 33 deletions, byte-identical to the staged file):

1. Delete the shared leg from the OR (`shopped: shoppedPersonal || shoppedShared` →
   `shopped: shoppedPersonal`). First attempt produced `TS6133: 'shoppedShared' is
   declared but its value is never read` — the same `noUnusedLocals` trap already logged
   for `Collections.x`, here on a destructured `Promise.all` result. Neutralised instead
   (`[shoppedShared].length > 99 ? true : shoppedPersonal`) → exactly ONE red:
   `shared-list activity sets shopped; another member's stamp and a prior day do not`.
   The new behaviour test is non-vacuous.
2. Swap the equality FIELD (`.where("lastActivityByUserId","==",userId)` →
   `.where("ownerId","==",userId)`) → **11/11 still green.** The fake's
   `makeActivityQuery.where()` maps any `op === "=="` to `userId` regardless of the field
   name, and stores `timeField` for the range ops without ever filtering on it. So the
   suite pins the collection (the fake's `collection()` throws on an unmodelled name, so a
   wrong collection reddens test 8) and the day window, but NOT the field names. The new
   `sharedShoppingListCompositeDeclared` test reads only the JSON, so it pins the INDEX
   side of the pair while the QUERY side drifts freely — and a query on `ownerId` matches
   no declared composite, throws FAILED_PRECONDITION, is swallowed by `safeProbe`, and
   re-zeroes exactly the flag BUT-1724/BUT-1761 each shipped to un-zero. Filed Medium
   (the SHIPPED query is correct — this is a coverage hole, not a live defect).
   Remediation: have the fake record the equality/range field names and throw on an
   unexpected one for the shared collection, or assert them in the index test.

Weaker point, filed Low: `sharedShoppedProbeFailureDegrades` case A stayed PASS under
mutation 1 — `flagA.shopped === false` holds trivially if the leg does not exist at all.
Case B (`flagB.shopped === true`) is what carries that test.

`messages` (conversationId ASC, sentAt ASC) composite and `items` fieldOverrides for
`addedByUserId` / `lastModifiedByUserId` (COLLECTION + COLLECTION_GROUP ASC) serving
`on-profile-updated.ts:217-220`. Noted but not owned by this review: a `fieldOverrides`
entry REPLACES the automatic single-field config for that field, so declaring only
ASCENDING drops the automatic DESCENDING and ARRAY_CONTAINS indexes for those two item

`{"flag":"shoppedShared","userIdHash":"30897b24242d","errName":"Error", ...}`. The

`lastActivityByUserId` stamp, so it is a lower bound; `contributorUserIds` would be worse

**Verdict: pass.** No Critical/High. Cost: +1 `limit(1)` query per user per run, issued
inside the existing `Promise.all`, so ~+1k reads/day at 1k active users and no added
wall-clock latency; the read-budget comment was updated 5→6 probes and 34k→35k reads.
Idempotency unchanged (deterministic doc ids, `set()` overwrite).

### 2026-07-30 — BUT-1770 item-level rename propagation + BUT-1755 createdAt sentinel + BUT-1722 refused-edit reason [Pattern discovered] [Bug fixed]

Scope handed to me (11 files, mostly Dart): `lib/models/unified/unified_shopping_list.dart`,
`lib/repositories/firebase/modules/shopping_list_permission_guards.dart`,
`lib/viewmodels/collaborative_shopping/shopping_item_operations_manager.dart`,
`lib/viewmodels/collaborative_shopping_viewmodel.dart`,
`lib/views/social/collaborative_shopping_view.dart`,
`functions/src/social/on-profile-updated.ts`, `firestore.indexes.json`, plus four test files.

**What shipped.** `on-profile-updated.ts` gained three legs under `if (nameChanged)`:
two `batchUpdateQueryPaginated(db.collectionGroup("items").where(<addedByUserId |
lastModifiedByUserId>, "==", userId), {<pairedDisplayName>: newName})`, and
`renameEmbeddedShoppingItems` — a `__name__`-cursor page loop (`EMBEDDED_ITEMS_PAGE_SIZE
= 50`) over `unified_shared_shopping_lists` `where("contributorUserIds","array-contains",
userId)`, running one `runTransaction` per list that re-reads, maps the `items` array,
rewrites only rows whose own `*ByUserId === userId`, and skips the write when nothing
changed. `firestore.indexes.json` gained COLLECTION + COLLECTION_GROUP ASC fieldOverrides
for `items.addedByUserId` and `items.lastModifiedByUserId`.

**Verified, not assumed:**
- `items` is shopping-only. The ONLY `match /items/{itemId}` blocks in `firestore.rules`
  are under `users/{userId}/unified_shopping_lists/{listId}` (line ~398) and
  `shared_content/{contentId}` (line ~788). No cross-feature blast radius for the
  collection group.
- No client query anywhere in `lib/` filters or orders on `addedByUserId` /
  `lastModifiedByUserId`, so declaring ASC-only fieldOverrides (which REPLACE automatic
  single-field indexing, dropping the automatic DESCENDING collection-scope entry) breaks
  nothing.
- The two other new index entries map to real queries in the same commit:
  `messages` (`conversationId` ASC + `sentAt` ASC) →
  `firebase_data_export_repository.dart:372`; `unified_shared_shopping_lists`
  (`lastActivityByUserId` ASC + `updatedAt` ASC) → `compute-feature-retention.ts:318`.
  Neither is needed by `on-profile-updated.ts`, whose legs all order by `__name__`.
- `npm run build` (tsc) clean. `npm run test:on-profile-updated` **10/10 PASS** (script
  name is `test:on-profile-updated`, NOT `test:profile-updated` as the family table's
  test-command column says — the table is wrong, npm suggested the right one).

**Finding (Medium) — rename scoping is a strict SUBSET of erasure scoping.**
`renameEmbeddedShoppingItems` uses `contributorUserIds array-contains` ALONE.
`deleteShoppingLists` (`account-deletion-cascade.ts:571-588`) unions FOUR queries over the
same collection — `memberPermissions.{uid} != null`, `ownerId == uid`,
`contributorUserIds array-contains uid`, `lastActivityByUserId == uid` — into one
`Map<docId, ref>`, with an in-file comment explaining exactly why one handle is not enough
("membership and ownership are the WRONG handles on their own, because both are things a
user can stop having while their name stays on the document"). The new function's own
docstring nevertheless says "The deletion cascade uses the same handle for the same
reason", which is false. Practical gap: rows added BEFORE BUT-1725 shipped, on lists never
touched since (the client unions the trail on every item write via `_withContributorTrail`
in `shopping_repository_routing_module.dart:352`), and not reached by
`backfillSharedListContributors` — which this file already records as structurally
unfinishable above its scan cap. Remediation: copy the cascade's four-query union + dedup.

**Finding (Medium) — the BUT-1755 sentinel is not round-trip stable.** Measured with a
throwaway `dart run` script:
```
utc=1970-01-01 00:00:00.000Z isUtc=true ms=0
local=1970-01-01 01:00:00.000 isUtc=false ms=0
utc == local -> false ; isAtSameMomentAs -> true
```
Dart's `DateTime.==` compares `isUtc` as well as the instant. `UnifiedShoppingList.
unknownCreatedAt = DateTime.utc(1970)` is written by `toFirestore()` as
`Timestamp.fromDate(...)` and read back through `SerializationUtils.parseDateTimeValue` →
`Timestamp.toDate()` → a LOCAL `DateTime`, so sentinel != round-tripped sentinel. It DOES
get persisted: `mutateCollaborativeList` does `transaction.set(_withContributorTrail(
mutated.toFirestore(), ...), SetOptions(merge:true))` on every collaborative item write,
and `toFirestore()` always includes `createdAt`. The owner branch of the
`unified_shared_shopping_lists` update rule carries no field constraints, so an owner's
tick stamps a legacy list's `createdAt` to epoch. A non-owner still holding a pre-stamp
in-memory entity then trips `proposed.createdAt != stored.createdAt` in
`requireNoPrivilegeEscalation` — the exact deadlock BUT-1755 set out to remove, in a
narrower window, complete with a false audit row. One-line fix:
`!proposed.createdAt.isAtSameMomentAs(stored.createdAt)`. Related: `fromJson` (model line
697) still defaults to `clock.now()` — the sentinel was applied to `fromMap` only.
(`fromJson` has no production caller today, tests only.)

**Non-vacuity, free.** `flutter test` on the new guard suite first came back 3 pass / 2
fail, and a rerun ~1 min later came back 5/5 with `git hash-object` identical on all three
files. The two reds were exactly the BUT-1755 tests ("a non-owner content edit on a list
with no stored createdAt is allowed", "the two parses agree on createdAt"). That is the
parallel-session mutate-and-restore window this file already documents — and it doubles as
proof those two tests DO redden when the sentinel default is reverted. Combined
model+guard run: 47 pass. `test/views/social/collaborative_shopping_view_test.dart`: 13
pass, including the three new BUT-1722 cases.

**BUT-1722 (Dart, no defect found).** `CollaborativeShoppingViewModel.
consumeItemOperationError()` reads-and-clears `ShoppingItemOperationsManager._error`
(guarded by `isDisposed`), and `_showFailureReason()` in the view falls back to `_vm.error`.
Correctly kept OUT of `_vm.error`, which drives the body's `LoadingStateBuilder` — routing
a refused tick there would blank the list (the BUT-1696 regression). The generic-fallback
widget test passes because the manager itself substitutes
`AppLocale.current.errorCouldNotUpdateItem` when `consumeMutationError()` returns null.

**Verdict: pass.** No Critical/High. Cost note for the deploy: the two COLLECTION_GROUP
fieldOverrides add an index entry per shopping-item write forever (small, but permanent),
and the embedded leg costs one transaction per contributed list per rename — sequential
within a page of 50, so a user on ~1000 shared lists spends ~100s of the 540s budget in
that leg alone; a concurrency pool is the upgrade if that ever becomes real.

### 2026-07-30/31 — Crash-salvage review: BUT-1766/1767/1768/1770/1761 (account-deletion-cascade, on-profile-updated, compute-feature-retention) [Bug fixed] [Cost finding]

Sprint 2026-07-30c was cut off by an infra outage before this gate ever ran; nothing was
committed. First-and-only pass against the uncommitted worktree. Scope: 8 files
(account-deletion-cascade.ts +416, request-account-deletion.ts +4, on-profile-updated.ts
+173, compute-feature-retention.ts +126/-42, three test files, firestore.indexes.json
+48, functions/package.json +1). `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean.
`test:account-deletion-cascade` 26/26 (new file, correctly registered in package.json —
the recurring wiring trap was NOT hit this time), `test:on-profile-updated` 11/11,
`test:compute-feature-retention` 11/11, `node scripts/check-test-registration.js` clean
(119 files, only the four already-accepted-debt integration warnings).

Two High findings, both new code, both a lost-update race against a concurrent edit by a
DIFFERENT, non-deleted user — the class the task brief specifically asked about:

1. `buildGroupDepartureUpdate` (account-deletion-cascade.ts) decides its `lastMessage.*`
   tombstone from `convoDoc.data()` captured by the OUTER
   `.where("participantIds","array-contains",uid).get()` query, then applies it via a plain
   `convoDoc.ref.update(...)` inside a bounded-10 `Promise.all`. A real message sent to that
   group between the query and this specific doc's write gets silently overwritten back to
   "[Raderad anvandare]" — and nothing re-fixes it until the NEXT message, since
   `sync-conversation-last-message.ts` only fires on a `messages/{id}` write, not a
   `conversations/{id}` write.
2. `scrubLastEditor` (same file, used by both `deleteRealtimeMenus` and
   `deleteRealtimeRecipes`) matches docs on `lastEditedBy == uid` at query time, then
   blind-overwrites `lastEditedBy`/`lastEditedByDisplayName` via `commitInChunks`'s plain
   `batch.update()`. A different collaborator editing the SAME realtime menu/recipe in that
   window (the whole point of "realtime") has their fresh `lastEditedBy` stamp reverted to
   "deleted".

Neither is caught by the 26/26 suite — its hand-rolled FakeFirestore has no concurrency
model at all (confirmed: no `runTransaction` implementation in that file; the two
`lastMessage` assertions — "the embedded lastMessage copy is tombstoned" /
"another member's lastMessage preview is left alone" — are both static, single-write
fixtures). The fix pattern already exists in the SAME file:
`deleteShoppingLists`'s per-list `runTransaction` (re-read inside, recompute, write) —
neither new call site uses it. Remediation given to the sprint: wrap each write in
`db.runTransaction`, re-read the doc, recompute the update (or skip) from the FRESH read.
Full reasoning archived as a principle in the main file (PII scrubbing section).

Everything else checked GOOD:
- firestore.indexes.json: the `items` collectionGroup fieldOverrides (4 fields:
  addedByUserId/lastModifiedByUserId/assignedToUserId/purchasedByUserId, each COLLECTION +
  COLLECTION_GROUP) exactly mirror the pre-existing `members`/`userId` precedent and are
  genuinely required by on-profile-updated.ts's new `collectionGroup("items")` legs — a
  dedicated test ("the collection-group index for every item attribution field is declared")
  pins it. `unified_shared_shopping_lists` (lastActivityByUserId ASC, updatedAt ASC) is
  correctly required by compute-feature-retention.ts's new `shoppedShared` probe (equality
  + range on different fields) and is the collection's only composite, so no
  reverse-direction check needed. ONE Medium/Low cost finding: the new `messages`
  (conversationId ASC, sentAt ASCENDING) composite is likely redundant —
  sync-conversation-last-message.ts:119 already needs (and the file already declares)
  (conversationId ASC, sentAt DESCENDING), and Firestore serves the opposite orderBy
  direction by scanning that same index in reverse; no query anywhere orders `sentAt` ASC.
  Recommend dropping it unless a specific future query needs it. Folded into a general
  principle (CI/ops section): always grep the collection name in firestore.indexes.json
  for an existing composite in the OPPOSITE orderBy direction before approving a new one.
- renameEmbeddedShoppingItems/renameItemsOnList (on-profile-updated.ts, BUT-1770): the
  per-list runTransaction IS the correct shape (re-reads `items` fresh inside the
  transaction, Firestore's optimistic-concurrency retry handles a genuine concurrent household
  edit) — this one does NOT have the bug above. Its test file is explicit and honest about the
  limit of its own fake: a code comment on the fake runTransaction
  ("BUT-1770: a PASSTHROUGH, exactly like FakeFirebaseFirestore on the Dart side... proves
  nothing about concurrency, and no test below claims otherwise") — exactly the discipline
  lessons-digest-testing.md asks for. One Medium note: renameEmbeddedShoppingItems's
  outer `for` loop has no try/catch around each renameItemsOnList call, so ONE list hitting
  ABORTED after Firestore's transaction retry budget is exhausted (real risk on a busy
  shared list) throws out of the whole pagination and skips every later page/list in that
  invocation — inconsistent with deleteShoppingLists's per-list try/catch-and-accumulate in
  the SAME sprint's other file. Self-heals on the next profile-name change, so not urgent, but
  worth fixing to match the established pattern.
- deleteRealtimeDocsWithChildren/removeRealtimeParticipation/removeVoteEntries: children
  strict-then-parent-best-effort ordering is correct (mirrors the deleteFamilyData
  household precedent), retry-safe (a partial run just re-scans on the next attempt), and the
  new probeResidualData legs (realtime_menus/realtime_recipes x ownerId/
  lastEditedBy/participantIds) are a strict superset of what the deleters actually clear —
  verified by reading both, not just the docstring's claim. Cost note: the child sweep is a
  fully SERIAL `for` loop (2 sequential reads per realtime doc, no Promise.all batching)
  unlike the messages leg's bounded-10 concurrency — low real risk given typical
  collaborative-menu/recipe fan-out per user is small, but flagged as a Medium
  cold-start/cost inconsistency worth a chunked-parallel upgrade if usage grows.
- probeResidualData's new legs correctly use uid_prefix/errCode/errName, never raw uid
  or err.message — the family convention holds.
- Wiring: realtime_menus step correctly added to request-account-deletion.ts's tier1
  array (BUT-1768's stated purpose — it previously had no tier entry at all). Auth-deletion
  ordering unchanged (cascade -> storage -> auth.deleteUser last), so the callable's own

Tangential discovery, OUT OF SCOPE (functions/src only) — handed off, not deep-reviewed:
while verifying removeVoteEntries's docstring claim ("the doc id is the slot's vote id...
despite what the rules comment suggests"), traced it end-to-end: MenuSlotVote.create mints

menu-voting feature is denied by rules for every user, which would mean the whole

it also means the account-deletion cascade's `votes.<uid>` residual concern is currently moot
(no live vote map entries to leave behind), which doesn't change the cascade's correctness

Verdict on the crash-salvage diff itself: not a blocking Critical, but the two lost-update
findings are real, concrete, self-consistent with an established fix pattern already in the

### 2026-07-30/31 — BUT-1766/1768 re-review: transaction-wrapping fix verified [Bug fixed] [Pattern discovered]

Follow-up to the 2026-07-30 crash-salvage review above (which found the two lost-update
findings in `buildGroupDepartureUpdate` and `scrubLastEditor`). Re-reviewed the fix diff
(`git diff HEAD -- functions/src/account/account-deletion-cascade.ts
functions/src/__tests__/account-deletion-cascade.test.ts`) after the sprint applied it.

Verified findings:
- `deleteMessages`'s group branch now does `await db.runTransaction(async (tx) => { const
  fresh = await tx.get(convoDoc.ref); if (!fresh.exists) return; tx.update(convoDoc.ref,
  buildGroupDepartureUpdate(fresh, uid)); })`. `buildGroupDepartureUpdate`'s param type
  changed `QueryDocumentSnapshot` -> `DocumentSnapshot` to accept `tx.get`'s result; grepped
  the whole `functions/src` tree and this is the ONLY call site, so the widened type breaks
  nothing else. The function's `lastMessage` branch already null-safes with `(convoDoc.data()
  ?? {})`, correct for a snapshot that can now be non-existent.
- `scrubLastEditor` rewritten to one `db.runTransaction` per doc, bounded to 10 concurrent via
  the same `chunkSize=10`/`Promise.all` shape `deleteMessages` already uses, re-checking
  `fresh.data()?.lastEditedBy !== uid` (return early if stale) before `tx.update`, each
  transaction wrapped in its own try/catch (best-effort, matches the `commitInChunks({strict:
  false})` semantics it replaces). Checked the bounded-10 loop for a race AGAINST ITSELF (part
  of the review brief): each of the 10 concurrent transactions in a wave targets a DISTINCT
  doc ref (`notOwned` is a deduped query result) — no two transactions in the same wave can
  ever touch the same document, so there is no such race.
- Both fixes derive every literal-value field from the FRESH transactional read only, never
  from the outer query snapshot's `.data()` (only `.ref` survives from the outer snapshot) —
  confirmed by reading, not just trusting the docstring. That is what makes real Firestore's
  transaction semantics (auto-retry on a conflicting write to a doc read inside the
  transaction) actually apply here; a fix that re-read fresh but still computed from the OLD
  object would not be fixed at all, and that's the exact bug shape to check for on any future
  transactional-fix review in this file.

Test-suite honesty check (the recurring "unsimulated fake stub must THROW, not answer"
concern, but the opposite finding this time): the new `FakeFirestore.runTransaction` added to
`account-deletion-cascade.test.ts` is a bare passthrough — `tx.get` reads the same in-memory
`docs` map `.update()`/`.get()` use, `tx.update`/`tx.delete` apply immediately via the same
`applyUpdate` helper the batch path uses, single-threaded so nothing can interleave — and its
own docstring says so ("nothing here proves the code resists an ACTUAL concurrent writer").
Grepped the suite for `race`/`concurrent`/`stale` — no scenario injects a concurrent write
between the outer query and the transactional re-read; all 26 checks (ran `npm run
test:account-deletion-cascade`, confirmed 26/26 live, not from the report) assert
NO-CONCURRENCY correctness (right fields scrubbed, right tombstone values, membership/lastMessage
logic right). That is real and valuable coverage for a DIFFERENT property (no regression in the
value-computation logic during the rewrite) — it is not, and structurally cannot be, coverage of
the concurrency-safety property the fix exists for. Concurrency-safety here is proven by code
inspection against documented Firestore Admin SDK transaction semantics, not by this suite.
Did not attempt to write a concurrency-injecting test or mutate the production file to
mutation-test the suite, per the reviewing user's explicit "do not edit files, report findings
only" instruction for this pass.

Also ran `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (no output) confirming the `DocumentSnapshot` type widening
compiles.

Verdict: PASS on both fixes — (a) no remaining stale-read path in either function, (b) the
FakeFirestore transaction stub is faithful for what it tests (field/value correctness) and
honestly does not claim more, (c) no new bug — grep-confirmed single call site for
`buildGroupDepartureUpdate`, no self-race in the bounded-10 `scrubLastEditor` loop.

### 2026-07-31 — BUT-1699: TTL policies for `notification_send_events` + `scheduled_notifications` [Pattern discovered] [Bug fixed]

Reviewed the change that declares both collections as `"ttl": true` `fieldOverrides` in
`firestore.indexes.json` (+ a new `firestore-ttl-policies.test.ts`, a package.json script,
two comment-only header rewrites, three doc corrections). Verdict: PASS, ship it.

**The load-bearing question was whether the mechanism works at all**, since two repo docs
asserted TTL is gcloud-only and the change's stated evidence was "13 policies are already
declared this way". That evidence is CIRCULAR and I had to discard it: `git show 9cd5b53c2`
says in its own commit body that the 13 were "staged by a parallel session; they mirror
policies that already exist in production" — i.e. synced DOWN from prod, never created by a
file deploy. So the file has never once created a TTL policy in this project, and this deploy
will be the first.

Proved the mechanism from the installed CLI instead (`firebase-tools@14.27.0`,
`C:/Users/malla/AppData/Roaming/npm/node_modules/firebase-tools/lib/firestore/api.js`):
- `deploy()` (l.140-149): for each spec, `exists = existingFieldOverrides.some(fieldMatchesSpec)`;
  not found → `patchField(project, field, databaseId)`.
- `patchField()` (l.296-330): PATCHes
  `/projects/{p}/databases/{db}/collectionGroups/{group}/fields/{fieldPath}` with
  `indexConfig.indexes`, and `if (spec.ttl) data = {...data, ttlConfig: {}}`. When
  `typeof spec.ttl !== "undefined"` it sends the patch WITHOUT an `updateMask`, so
  `ttlConfig` is applied; when ttl is undefined it patches with
  `updateMask: "indexConfig"`, which is what leaves an existing live policy untouched.
- `fieldMatchesSpec()` (l.408-421): `booleanXOR(!!field.ttlConfig, spec.ttl)` → mismatch
  re-patches; live ttlConfig + undefined spec.ttl only logs a bullet.
- Corollary nobody had written down: an explicit `"ttl": false` DISABLES a live policy with
  no `--force`, because the mask is dropped and `ttlConfig` is simply absent from the body.
- `--force` (l.117-155) is the separate danger: `fieldOverridesToDelete` matches by
  collectionGroup+fieldPath only, so every live override absent from the file is deleted.
  `.github/workflows/deploy-firebase.yml` `deploy_one()` runs `--non-interactive`, no

### 2026-08-01 — BUT-1781 tagging/backend sprint: the `recipes` dead-path sweep [Bug fixed] [Pattern discovered]

Scope reviewed (7 files): `functions/src/ingredients/on-ingredient-soft-deleted.ts`,
`functions/src/ingredients/on-ingredient-properties-changed.ts`,
`functions/src/cleanup/cleanup-deleted-ingredients.ts`, `firestore.indexes.json`,
`lib/services/unified/operations/modules/rating_statistics.dart`,
`lib/services/unified/operations/modules/recipe_social_stats.dart`,
`test/unit/services/unified/operations/modules/rating_statistics_denormalization_test.dart`.
Verdict: FAIL (1 Critical, 2 High).

**The ticket's premise is real.** Recipes live only at `users/{uid}/recipes/{recipeId}`
(`firestore.rules:356`, plus the admin-only collection-group catch-all at `:2217`); every
`db.collection("recipes")` read in the repo matched zero docs. Both ingredient cascades and
the weekly stale-recipe monitor were dead on arrival for that reason. The swap to
`collectionGroup("recipes")` is correct, `core` IS a nested map
(`recipe_serialization.dart:50` writes `'core': recipe.core.toFirestore()`), so the
`core.ingredientsNormalized` / `core.tagResult.generatorVersion` field paths are right, and
the two new `fieldOverrides` (CONTAINS + COLLECTION_GROUP; ASC/DESC COLLECTION + ASC
COLLECTION_GROUP) are the correct and non-lossy shape — the auto single-field config for
each field is a strict subset, no pre-existing `recipes` override to clobber
(`node -e` over the file: 52 indexes / 28 fieldOverrides, only these two for `recipes`),
and a single-field COLLECTION_GROUP index carries the trailing `__name__ ASC` that
`batchUpdateQueryPaginated`'s `orderBy(documentId())` needs. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

**Critical — the Dart half is dead on arrival, and its test asserts the denied write.**
`rating_statistics.dart` split one always-failing batch into two sequential awaits. Old
code: `batch.set(recipe_social_stats/…)` + `batch.update(recipes/{id})` — the update on a
non-existent top-level doc aborted the WHOLE batch, so the stats write never landed either.
New code writes `recipe_social_stats` FIRST (`:192` delete / `:209` set) and calls
`_denormalizeOntoRecipe` second (`:193`/`:218`). But `firestore.rules:2506-2508` is
`match /recipe_social_stats/{recipeId} { allow read: if isAuthenticated(); allow create,
update, delete: if false; }` — server-only. So in production the first await throws
`permission-denied`, the outer `catch` rethrows (`:232`), and the denormalization (the whole
point of the ticket) never runs. `fake_cloud_firestore` evaluates no rules, so
`rating_statistics_denormalization_test.dart:107-112` asserts the client CAN write that
collection and goes green. Second-order: `functions/src/ratings/update-recipe-rating-stats.ts`
(wired `index.ts:371` on `recipe_ratings/{ratingId}`) OWNS that doc and folds
`family_ratings` where `memberType == "profile"` into it; the client's numbers are
account-only, and its empty-branch `delete()` would destroy an aggregate still holding
family-diner votes. Fix: delete both `statsRef` writes from the client; keep the
`recipe_ratings` query (it feeds the denorm values) and `_denormalizeOntoRecipe` alone.

**High — `bulkMarkForRetagging` was left on the dead path.** `admin/bulk-retag.ts:252` and
`:421` still do `getDb().collection("recipes")`. It is an EXPORTED callable
(`index.ts:127`), i.e. the operator escape hatch that clears exactly the `stale-ingredient`
markers the fixed cascades now write, and it silently retags 0 recipes and reports
`getRetagStatus` counts of 0. Same disease, same sprint, one file away.

**High — the 60s platform kill.** `setGlobalOptions` (`index.ts:41`) sets only `region`, so
these v2 event functions run at the 60s default while `CASCADE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120000`
(`shared/with-timeout.ts:8`). The guard can never fire; the platform kills the instance
first, with no error log, a partially-applied cascade, no `retry: true` and no resume
cursor (`batchUpdateQueryPaginated` restarts at page 1). Inert while the query matched
nothing; live now that a common ingredient ("salt") matches most of the corpus across all
users.

**Medium — the monitor still under-reports its sibling's output.**
`on-ingredient-properties-changed.ts:135` stamps `"stale-properties"`;
`cleanup-deleted-ingredients.ts:144,150,187,193` counts only `stale-ingredient` + `failed`,
and `offline_user_storage.dart:100-107`'s narrow `_needsRetagging` matches only
`failed`/`pending`/`stale-ingredient`. The generic `TagResult.needsRetagging`
(`tag_result.dart:791`, `!= kTagGeneratorVersion`) DOES catch it, so this is a monitoring +
offline-sync-queue gap, not a silent-allergen-staleness one — checked before filing it
higher.

**Mid-review file movement (the documented parallel-session pattern).** First run of
`rating_statistics_denormalization_test.dart` was 1/3 (`core.ratingCount` null; empty-branch
left `3`). Standalone probes of every suspected cause passed — `fake_cloud_firestore`
handles dotted `update()` paths, int-keyed maps and `FieldValue.delete()` on a nested path
fine, and a hand-built replica of both cases went green against the real SUT. Re-ran the
real file with `git hash-object` bracketing: 3/3 green, test `1c99ac42…`, SUT `baf26660…`,
identical before and after. So the red was against bytes a parallel session was mid-edit on,
per the existing rule — report the green run against the hashed bytes, don't write up the red.
`flutter analyze` on the three Dart files: clean.

### 2026-08-01 — BUT-1788 `leaveGroupConversation` review [Bug found]

Scope: `functions/src/messaging/leave-group-conversation.ts` (new, `git hash-object`
`6127e892c0f7523680faa92e49c5f259e17f791d`), its test (`aae5c611…`),
`app-check-enforcement.test.ts`, `index.ts`, `functions/package.json`, plus the Dart
call-site (`conversation_mutation_module.dart`, `firebase_messaging_repository.dart`)
and its unit test.

**The ticket itself is real and correctly diagnosed.** `firestore.rules:1532-1535` denies
every client `conversations` update whose diff touches `participantIds`, so both "leave
group" and admin "remove member" have never landed; the follow-up `senderId:"system"`
message was refused by the `messages` create rule (`rules:1560-1562`) too. Moving the
write to an Admin-SDK callable and leaving the rule closed is the right shape — a rule
permissive enough to shrink `participantIds` cannot express "by exactly one entry, only
your own uid unless admin", so it would be a group-takeover primitive.

Verified green, both lanes: `npm run test:leave-group-conversation` 20/20,
`npm run test:app-check-enforcement` 16/16 (the new callable is classified `USER_FACING`),
`npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0, `node scripts/check-test-registration.js` OK (121 files),
`test:leave-group-conversation` present in `package.json` so `run-ci-unit-tests.js`
auto-discovers it and `CI_EXCLUDE` is empty. Dart: `flutter test
test/unit/repositories/firebase/modules/conversation_mutation_module_test.dart` 15 passed
/1 pre-existing skip; `flutter analyze` on the three Dart files clean. First `Read` of the
test file came back truncated at line 314 of 476 (mid-write by the sprint session) and
made the whole fake-Firestore orchestration half look like dead code — `wc -l` + re-read
settled it. Cross-checked field parity by hand: the CF's `messages` payload matches
`MessageDto.toFirestore` name-for-name (`reactions` optional in `fromMap`),
`MessageType.system`/`MessageStatus.delivered` exist, the mirror paths
`conversations/{id}/participants/{uid}` and `users/{uid}/conversation_memberships/{id}`
match `FirestoreCollections.participants`/`.userConversationMemberships`, and the client's
`isAdmin` (`group_detail_viewmodel.dart:99-103`, `metadata['creatorId'] == currentUserId`)
matches the server's admin check exactly. Also confirmed the module-scope
`const db = admin.firestore()` is the house pattern (4 siblings) and safe because TS emits
`export … from` requires in SOURCE order, after `admin.initializeApp()`; and that an
`HttpsError` thrown inside `runTransaction` is NOT retried — `isRetryableTransactionError`
(`@google-cloud/firestore/build/src/transaction.js:582-592`) switches on NUMERIC gRPC codes
while `HttpsError.code` is the string `"not-found"`, so no wasted read fan-out.

**High — the callable is an existence/membership ORACLE for non-members.** The read
happens before any caller-membership check, and the three branches are distinguishable to
a total outsider probing an arbitrary `conversationId`:
`not-found` (doc missing) / `failed-precondition` "Cannot remove participants from a direct
conversation" (a 1:1 exists) / `{success:true, removed:false, remainingParticipants:N}` —
because `authorizeDeparture` (lines 139-143) reaches `targetUid === callerUid` and returns
`noop` for a caller who was never a participant, and the noop branch returns the group's
REAL member count (line 263). Weaponisable because both halves are public: direct
conversation ids are deterministic (`direct_${sortedUid1}_${sortedUid2}`,
`conversation_mutation_module.dart:57`) and every uid is enumerable — `public_profiles`
doc id IS the uid and `allow read: if isAuthenticated()` (`firestore.rules:609-611`). So
any signed-in account can answer "does A DM B?" for arbitrary A,B, i.e. reconstruct the
private messaging graph, and can read the member count of any group whose id it learns.
The suite cannot see it: the leak is exactly the shape of the legitimate idempotent
retry (`verdict("gone","gone")` → noop), which is why the green idempotency case reads as
proof of correctness. Fix: gate on `participantIds.includes(callerUid)` immediately after
the read and return ONE uniform `{removed:false, remaining:0}` for both `!snap.exists` and
non-member — a genuine post-leave retry is a non-member too, so idempotency survives.

**Medium — twin class untouched in the same file.** `addParticipants`
(`conversation_mutation_module.dart:243-291`) still rebuilds `participantIds` client-side
(`updateFn` at :271) and still sends a `Message.system` (:286-290) — denied by the SAME two
rules the new docstring quotes. "Add member to group" is as broken as remove was; the file
now reads as fixed. Pre-existing, not introduced by the diff.

**Medium — no rate limit.** `setProfileSearchability:72` and `verify-signup-age:145` both
call `enforceRateLimit`; the new callable has nothing, so the probing loop above is
unmetered and every call bills a doc read. (`acceptFriendRequest` is also bare, so the
family convention is mixed, not unanimous.)

**Low — orphan on the last departure.** When the final member leaves, `participantIds`
becomes `[]`; `rules:1496` (read) and `:1538` (delete) both require membership, so no
client can ever read or delete the doc again, while `syncConversationLastMessage` keeps
writing `lastMessage` to it. No cleanup leg anywhere.

**Low — count/doc disagreement.** `remainingParticipants` is computed off the SANITISED
list while `arrayRemove` leaves junk entries in the stored array. The padded-list test
asserts `1` where the document actually holds `["b","__x__"]`.

**Info — server-side Swedish string.** `departureMessage` (line 66-68) hardcodes
`"${name} har lämnat gruppen"`, byte-matching `chatParticipantLeft` in `app_sv.arb:9415`
today, with no lockstep guard and no locale awareness. Same for the locally-duplicated
`PER_USER_CONVERSATION_MAPS` (documented rationale — a map added to the cascade's copy
drifts silently).

### 2026-08-01 — BUT-1791 / BUT-1789 review: probe the previous completed UTC day; feature-retention rows join the GDPR cascade
[Pattern discovered] [Bug fixed]

Scope: `functions/src/analytics/compute-feature-retention.ts`,
`functions/src/__tests__/compute-feature-retention.test.ts`,
`functions/src/account/account-deletion-cascade.ts`,
`functions/src/account/request-account-deletion.ts`,
`functions/src/__tests__/account-deletion-cascade.test.ts`, plus both accepted-deviation files.

Hashes (`git hash-object`, identical before and after every run — no mid-review mutation):
compute-feature-retention.ts `1b3c41be3c975c5fe2d3002a704dc665f91e2c10`;
compute-feature-retention.test.ts `c2a3e33fc3073335a304303e922c356cb41b0f1e`;
account-deletion-cascade.ts `0fd4edcd11133a1d0caac2ff16dfa90aa480a899`;
account-deletion-cascade.test.ts `91a81744b99f62526ed6e177f179bd32e3775162`;
request-account-deletion.ts `bb22fbecea02368102c841f4e4bbfc772d202921`.

**BUT-1791.** The job is scheduled `30 4 * * *` UTC and probed `startOfUtcDay(now)` — the day
it was standing in — so its window was 00:00–04:30 of the run day and no later run ever
revisited that day (the next run asked about the next day). All five flags — `cooked`,
`imported`, `shared`, `mealPlanned`, `shopped` — measured the small hours while reading as a
whole day. Fix is one line, `probeStartMs = startOfUtcDay(nowMs) - MS_PER_DAY`, with
`dateStr`, `dayStart`/`dayEnd`, the 27 rollup offsets and `activeCutoff` all re-derived from
that single base (the cutoff therefore moves one day earlier — slightly wider user scan, no
other effect). The suite could not have caught it: every case ran `now = 08:00Z` against
activity at `06:00Z`, i.e. a run AFTER the activity, which the 04:30 schedule never performs.
The new case `probesPreviousCompletedUtcDay` stages the real hour (04:30Z) with an evening
activity (29th 20:00Z, must count) and a run-day activity (30th 02:00Z, must not), and asserts
nothing is written under the run day at all.

Verification run: `npm run test:compute-feature-retention` → 12/12. Non-vacuity by mutation
(shadow copy, see below): reverting `probeStartMs` to `startOfUtcDay(nowMs)` → 3/12, with the
new case among the 9 reds.

Header claims checked against code rather than read: `MONITORED_SERIES` in
`detect-anomalies.ts` is still the five `daily-snapshots.ts` series (`import_health_totalFailure`,
`recipes_total`, `parsing_corrections_total`, `ops_totalEvents`, `feedback_total`) — no
retention flag is watched, so the across-the-board step change cannot raise a z-score alert.
The one-day dashboard lag is safe for the only in-repo consumer:
`lib/repositories/engagement_repository.dart` orders `daily` by `documentId` descending and
takes 14, so a missing "today" doc is invisible to it; an out-of-repo consumer keyed on today's
date would see a hole for one day (the admin dashboard is a separate app — not verified here).

**BUT-1789.** `analytics/feature_retention/users/{uid}_{yyyy-mm-dd}` is one behavioural row per
active day carrying the uid in the id and in a `userId` field, and nothing deleted it: no
cascade step, no TTL, no deviation entry. It is invisible to BOTH of `probeResidualData`'s
structural loops — the top-level `where("userId","==",uid)` list and the `users/{uid}/…`
subcollection list — because it is a subcollection under an analytics DOCUMENT. New
`deleteFeatureRetentionFlags` (tier 1, `where("userId","==",uid)` → `batchDeleteAll`) plus a
`count()` probe leg on the same handle, appended with its own try/catch. Deleter and probe use
the identical handle, so the deleter stays a superset.

Why not a TTL, and this is the reusable half: TTL `fieldOverrides` are COLLECTION-GROUP scoped
and this subcollection's collection ID is `users` — the same id as the top-level profile
collection — so the policy would arm a delete over real user documents. Checked the same
collision on the index side: `firestore.indexes.json` has no `fieldOverrides` and no composite
for collectionGroup `users`, so the automatic single-field index serves the deleter's equality
query, and no `collectionGroup("users")` query exists anywhere in `functions/src` or `lib/`
that these rows could pollute.

Verification: `npm run test:account-deletion-cascade` → 29/29. Mutation (shadow copy) swapping
the deleter's `where("userId", …)` for `ownerId` → 28/29, reddening exactly "every
feature-retention day of the deleted user is erased". `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 over the whole
tree.

**Technique worth keeping: shadow-copy mutation.** The worktree had ~45 modified files from a
parallel sprint session, so in-place mutate-and-restore was too dangerous. Instead: copy the
SUT to `src/<dir>/_cfs_mut_<x>.ts` with the mutation applied (asserting the substitution
actually landed), copy the suite to `src/__tests__/_cfs_mut_<x>.test.ts` with only its
import/`require` path rewritten, run the copy, delete both, `git status --porcelain` to prove
nothing tracked moved. Relative imports resolve unchanged because the copy sits in the same
directory, and there is no restore step that can fail half-way.

**Findings filed** (none Critical/High, verdict pass): the new `probeResidualData` leg has no
unit case and the cascade suite's fake `where()` returns no `count()`, so the probe/deleter
coupling is not provable in that lane (Medium); `logger.error("compute_feature_retention_failed",
{ err })` at the schedule wrapper still nests the Error in the payload → `err: {}`, while this
same file's `safeProbe` already uses the `errCode`/`errName` shape (Low, pre-existing);
`deleteFeatureRetentionFlags` does an unbounded `.get()` over a collection that grows one doc
per active day forever with no TTL (Low); and a narrow race where the 04:30 job writes a flag
row for a user whose cascade completed between the users-page read and the flag write, leaving
a row no probe or future run clears (Low — `onUserDeleted` in `cleanup/on-user-deleted.ts` does
social cleanup only and would be the cheap place for a second sweep).

### 2026-08-01 — BUT-1781 re-review: ingredient cascades repointed to `collectionGroup("recipes")` [Bug fixed] [Cost finding]

Re-reviewed the working tree after automated fixes, file set:
`functions/src/ingredients/on-ingredient-soft-deleted.ts`,
`functions/src/ingredients/on-ingredient-properties-changed.ts`,
`functions/src/cleanup/cleanup-deleted-ingredients.ts`, `firestore.indexes.json`,
plus the Dart half (`rating_statistics.dart`, `recipe_social_stats.dart` and the new
`rating_statistics_denormalization_test.dart`). Verdict: pass, no Critical/High.

What the diff does. Both ingredient triggers move `db.collection(Collections.recipes)` →
`db.collectionGroup(Collections.recipes)` (soft-deleted `:90`, properties-changed `:138`) and
gain explicit `timeoutSeconds: CASCADE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` + `memory: "512MiB"` options — the
trigger signature changes from the string form to the options-object form.
`shared/with-timeout.ts` now exports the guard and the platform limit as a pair
(`CASCADE_TIMEOUT_MS = 500000`, `CASCADE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 540`); the old 120000 against the
v2 event default of 60s was inert. `cleanup-deleted-ingredients.ts` factors the four
duplicated stale counts into `STALE_TAG_MARKERS = ["stale-ingredient","stale-properties"]` +
`countByMarkers()` over `collectionGroup("recipes")`, fixing a real drift: the monitor and the
admin-stats callable both counted only `stale-ingredient`, so the properties cascade — the
ALLERGEN-relevant one — was invisible to the dashboard meant to watch it.
`firestore.indexes.json` gains three `recipes` fieldOverrides (`core.ingredientsNormalized`
CONTAINS COLLECTION+COLLECTION_GROUP; `core.tagResult.generatorVersion` and `core.createdBy`
ASC/DESC COLLECTION + ASC COLLECTION_GROUP, the latter for `admin/bulk-retag.ts`).

Verified positives (each checked against code, not prose):
- Blast radius of the collection group is nil beyond the intended set: `grep "match /recipes"
  firestore.rules` → only `users/{uid}/recipes/{recipeId}` at `:356` and the admin-only
  read-only catch-all `match /{path=**}/recipes/{recipeId}` at `:2217`.
- `admin/bulk-retag.ts` — flagged in this file as an UNSWEPT consumer — is now swept via a
  `recipesGroup()` helper at `:33`, used at `:268` and `:434`.
  `grep -rn 'collection("recipes")' functions/src` leaves `compute-feature-retention.ts:347`,
  `canonical-rating-aggregation.ts:157` and `send-activity-digest.ts:83` (all correctly chained
  off `.collection("users").doc(uid)`) plus `account-deletion-cascade.ts:413`, the deliberate
  legacy net beside the real subcollection read at `:412`.
- Pagination cursor invariant holds: `batchUpdateQueryPaginated` orders by `__name__` and the
  update touches only `core.tagResult.generatorVersion`, never the filtered
  `core.ingredientsNormalized` nor the doc id.
- `isValidTagResult` (`firestore.rules:157`) does not constrain `generatorVersion` VALUES, so an
  admin-SDK `stale-*` stamp cannot lock the owner out of their next client update. A stub
  `tagResult` created on a recipe that had none still passes `keys().hasOnly(...)`.
- End-to-end marker chain consistent: producers write both markers → `STALE_TAG_MARKERS` counts
  both → `offline_user_storage._needsRetagging:105-113` accepts both → `TagResult.needsRetagging
  :791-799` returns true via version mismatch → `isAllUnknown:777` is `generatorVersion ==
  'all_unknown'`, version-string based, so the stub is not skipped by `retagging_scheduler`.
- `firestore.indexes.json` parses, no duplicate `recipes` fieldOverrides, and the 15-collection
  TTL set tripwire is untouched.

Commands run: `npm run build` (clean); `npx ts-node src/__tests__/firestore-ttl-policies.test.ts`
5/5; `pool-aggregation` 9/9; `cleanup-expired-social-requests` 2/2; `on-profile-updated` 11/11
(the last three all read `firestore.indexes.json`, so they are the regression check on the index
edit); `flutter test .../rating_statistics_denormalization_test.dart` 6/6.

Findings filed (all Medium or below):
1. NO TEST anywhere pins any of this. There is no `test:*` script for either ingredient cascade
   or for `cleanup-deleted-ingredients.ts`, and no assertion over the three new fieldOverrides.
   A regression from `collectionGroup(` back to `collection(`, or a dropped index entry, reddens
   nothing — which is precisely the silent-zero class BUT-1781 exists to fix. This is the single
   most important follow-up.
2. Deploy ordering: indexes must be READY before the functions ship, else every query
   FAILED_PRECONDITIONs and the trigger's catch-and-rethrow drops the cascade (no `retry:true`).
3. `batchUpdateQueryPaginated` uses `batch.update()`; one concurrently deleted recipe fails the
   whole 500-doc chunk with NOT_FOUND, the throw escapes `cascadeOperation`, and with no retry
   and no persisted cursor every later page is silently never marked. Same on a 500s guard fire.
4. Cost: these are the first invocations that will EVER match documents. A property edit on
   "salt"/"mjöl" stamps every matching recipe across every user (1 write each) and each stamped
   recipe then costs a client-side re-tag. `512MiB` doubles the per-ms rate of both triggers vs
   the 256MiB default, and the three new COLLECTION_GROUP single-field entries add index-write
   cost to every recipe write from now on. All defensible; be deliberate before a bulk sync.
5. `withTimeout` races, it does not cancel — writes continue for ~40s after the log says
   "timed out".
6. Dart side (out of my usual scope, reviewed on request): `rating_statistics.dart` now writes
   `users/{uid}/recipes/{id}` under `core.*` instead of a top-level `recipes` doc, and stops

only (verified — no update trigger), so a dormant group keeps the name forever. Fix: scrub the
mirror first, then the handle-clearing write, and skip clearing the handle for any conversation
whose mirror write failed. Folded into the "destroy the retry handle LAST" principle.
